name: Machine Learning
description: Classical machine learning from regression to clustering, with the maths behind it and real projects.

nodes.name: The ML workflow
nodes.desc: Supervised versus unsupervised learning, features and labels, train/test splits, and the problem → data → model → evaluation loop.
nodes.summary: You will understand the main types of machine learning and be able to frame a problem as features, labels and a train-test evaluation loop.
topics: The problem, data, model, evaluation loop

nodes.name: Data preprocessing
nodes.desc: Cleaning data, handling missing values, encoding categories, and feature scaling with pandas and scikit-learn.
nodes.summary: You will be able to clean a raw dataset, handle missing values, encode categories and scale features with pandas and scikit-learn.
topics: Inspecting and cleaning data with pandas
Fitting transformers on training data only

nodes.name: Linear regression
nodes.desc: Least squares as a loss, the normal equations, and interpreting coefficients.
nodes.summary: You will be able to fit linear regression by least squares, derive the normal equations and interpret the learned coefficients.
topics: Hypothesis and mean squared error loss

nodes.name: House price model
nodes.desc: Build a regression model on a housing dataset: clean the data, fit linear regression, and report test error.
nodes.summary: You will build a house price regression model, from cleaning the data to fitting linear regression and reporting test error.
topics: Measuring RMSE on a test set

nodes.name: Gradient descent
nodes.desc: Batch, stochastic and mini-batch gradient descent; learning rates and convergence.
nodes.summary: You will be able to train models with batch, stochastic and mini-batch gradient descent and choose a learning rate that converges.

nodes.name: Bias–variance
nodes.desc: Underfitting and overfitting, the bias–variance trade-off and learning curves.
nodes.summary: You will be able to diagnose underfitting and overfitting using the bias-variance trade-off and learning curves.

nodes.name: Regularisation
nodes.desc: Ridge (L2) and lasso (L1) penalties and how they control model complexity.
nodes.summary: You will be able to control model complexity with ridge and lasso penalties and explain how they affect coefficients.
topics: Ridge regression and the L2 penalty
Sparsity and feature selection with lasso

nodes.name: Model evaluation
nodes.desc: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC curves, confusion matrices and k-fold cross-validation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to evaluate models with the right metrics and estimate generalisation reliably with k-fold cross-validation.

nodes.name: Logistic regression
nodes.desc: The sigmoid, cross-entropy loss and decision boundaries for binary classification.
nodes.summary: You will be able to train logistic regression for binary classification and interpret its probabilities and decision boundary.

nodes.name: Naive Bayes
nodes.desc: Generative classification with Bayes' rule and the conditional-independence assumption.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build generative classifiers with Bayes' rule and the naive conditional-independence assumption.

nodes.name: k-nearest neighbours
nodes.desc: Distance-based classification, choosing k and the curse of dimensionality.
nodes.summary: You will be able to classify with k-nearest neighbours, choose k and a distance metric, and explain the curse of dimensionality.

nodes.name: Decision trees
nodes.desc: Splitting on entropy and information gain or Gini impurity, and pruning.
nodes.summary: You will be able to grow decision trees by choosing splits with entropy or Gini impurity and prune them to avoid overfitting.

nodes.name: SVMs & perceptron
nodes.desc: The perceptron, maximum-margin classifiers, support vectors and the kernel trick.
nodes.summary: You will understand the perceptron and maximum-margin classifiers and be able to use kernels for non-linear decision boundaries.
topics: Soft margins and the C parameter
The kernel trick and RBF kernels

nodes.name: Spam classifier
nodes.desc: Build a text classifier with bag-of-words features, compare naive Bayes and logistic regression, and evaluate with precision and recall.
nodes.summary: You will build a spam classifier with bag-of-words features and compare naive Bayes and logistic regression using precision and recall.

nodes.name: k-means clustering
nodes.desc: k-means, initialisation, choosing k and the elbow method.
nodes.summary: You will be able to cluster unlabelled data with k-means, initialise it well and choose the number of clusters.

nodes.name: Hierarchical clusters
nodes.desc: Agglomerative clustering, single and complete linkage, and dendrograms.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build agglomerative clusterings, compare linkage criteria and read dendrograms to pick clusters.

nodes.name: PCA
nodes.desc: Dimensionality reduction with principal components, explained variance and LDA.
nodes.summary: You will be able to reduce dimensionality with principal component analysis and contrast it with supervised LDA.

nodes.name: Customer segments
nodes.desc: Cluster a customer dataset, reduce it with PCA to visualise the groups, and describe each segment.
nodes.summary: You will cluster a customer dataset, visualise the groups with PCA and describe what distinguishes each segment.

nodes.name: Ensembles
nodes.desc: Bagging, random forests and gradient boosting.
nodes.summary: You will be able to combine models with bagging, random forests and gradient boosting to improve predictive accuracy.

nodes.name: Feature engineering
nodes.desc: Building informative features, feature selection, pipelines and avoiding data leakage.
nodes.summary: You will be able to create informative features, select useful ones and build pipelines that avoid data leakage.

nodes.name: Hyperparameter tuning
nodes.desc: Grid and random search with cross-validation, and keeping a clean held-out test set.
nodes.summary: You will be able to tune hyperparameters with grid and random search under cross-validation while keeping a clean held-out test set.

nodes.name: End-to-end pipeline
nodes.desc: Take a tabular competition dataset from raw CSV to a tuned ensemble with a reproducible pipeline and a short written report.
nodes.summary: You will take a tabular dataset from raw CSV to a tuned, reproducible ensemble model and write a short report on the results.
